proof:
Source: Steps 1–2 of the supplied proof of variation_matrix_det_derivatives_at_one (the Leibniz-expansion argument behind the derivative form of Simon's expansion of det(I + A), Simon Ch. 2, p. 62).

Notation. Perm(ι) is the finite group of permutations of ι, and sgn(σ) ∈ {1, −1} is the sign of σ, viewed as the real number ((sgn σ : ℤ) : ℝ). For m ∈ ι, Π_{j≠m} denotes the product over the finite set ι∖{m} (Finset.univ.erase m). "f has derivative c at x" means HasDerivAt f c x.

1. Leibniz expansion. For every real ι×ι matrix M, det M = Σ_{σ∈Perm(ι)} sgn(σ) · Π_{i∈ι} M_{σ(i) i} (Matrix.det_apply', where ε σ denotes ((sgn σ : ℤ) : ℝ)). Apply this to M = G(t) for every real t. Then the functions t ↦ det G(t) and F(t) := Σ_σ sgn(σ) · Π_{i∈ι} G(t)_{σ(i) i} are equal (function extensionality). So it suffices to prove that F has derivative L := Σ_σ sgn(σ) · Σ_{m∈ι} (Π_{j≠m} G(x)_{σ(j) j}) · H_{σ(m) m} at x.

2. One permutation. Fix σ ∈ Perm(ι). For i ∈ ι put f_i(t) := G(t)_{σ(i) i}. The hypothesis for the entry (σ(i), i) says that f_i has derivative H_{σ(i) i} at x. The product rule for a finite product of real functions over the finite set ι (HasDerivAt.fun_finsetProd with u = Finset.univ) now applies. It shows that t ↦ Π_{i∈ι} f_i(t) has derivative Σ_{m∈ι} (Π_{j∈ι∖{m}} f_j(x)) · H_{σ(m) m} at x. In ℝ the scalar action • of that lemma is multiplication (smul_eq_mul). Since f_j(x) = G(x)_{σ(j) j}, this derivative is Σ_m (Π_{j≠m} G(x)_{σ(j) j}) · H_{σ(m) m}.

3. Constant factor. Multiply by the constant real number sgn(σ) (HasDerivAt.const_mul). Then t ↦ sgn(σ) · Π_{i∈ι} G(t)_{σ(i) i} has derivative sgn(σ) · Σ_m (Π_{j≠m} G(x)_{σ(j) j}) · H_{σ(m) m} at x.

4. Sum over permutations. Perm(ι) is finite. Apply the sum rule for a finite sum of functions (HasDerivAt.fun_sum over Finset.univ of Perm(ι)) to the functions of step 3. So F has derivative Σ_σ sgn(σ) · Σ_m (Π_{j≠m} G(x)_{σ(j) j}) · H_{σ(m) m} = L at x.

5. By steps 1 and 4, t ↦ det G(t) has derivative L at x, which is the claim. The argument is uniform in ι, including ι = ∅. Then Perm(ι) = {id}, the product over ι is empty (equal to 1) and the inner sum over m is empty (equal to 0).
key_steps: Leibniz expansion det M = Σ_σ sgn σ Π_i M_{σ(i)i} (Matrix.det_apply'), so t ↦ det G(t) equals F(t) := Σ_σ sgn σ Π_i G(t)_{σ(i)i}.
For fixed σ, the finite product rule (HasDerivAt.fun_finsetProd over Finset.univ) shows that t ↦ Π_i G(t)_{σ(i)i} has derivative Σ_m (Π_{j≠m} G(x)_{σ(j)j}) H_{σ(m)m} at x.
The constant-multiple and finite-sum rules over Perm(ι) give F′(x) = Σ_σ sgn σ Σ_m (Π_{j≠m} G(x)_{σ(j)j}) H_{σ(m)m}. Since F = det ∘ G, this is the claim.
